cards.text: Grab a seat, friend, we're reading somebody else's mail, and for once it's ALLOWED. Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, writes this letter with Timothy, his brother in the faith (Colossians 1:1). It goes to the believers in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia (Acts 16:12).

cards.question: Right at the top of the letter, Paul and Timothy call themselves ___ of Christ Jesus

cards.text: The letter is for all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, and the overseers and deacons get a shout-out too, so the WHOLE group chat is on this one. Then Paul opens with "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ."

cards.question: Paul says something happens every time he remembers the believers at Philippi. What does he do?
True or false: Paul says his prayers for the believers at Philippi are heavy with worry.

cards.text: Then Paul tells them why he prays with so much joy. It goes back to the very first day, and it's still going NOW, which is more than I can say for my first batch of cookies.

cards.question: From the first day until now, the believers at Philippi have been Paul's ___ in the gospel

cards.text: Next, Paul says what he's sure of: God began a good work in these believers. Me? I started building a cooling rack in the back of the bakery a while ago, and friend… it's a shelf now. It's always gonna be a shelf.

cards.question: Paul is confident about the good work God began in the believers at Philippi. What will God do with it?

answers.text: Leave the rest up to them

cards.text: Paul says it's right for him to feel this way, because he has them in his heart. And he's writing all this from CHAINS, friend, while I spent years in a junk drawer and couldn't manage a "hi."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that in his chains and in his defense of the gospel, the believers at Philippi are all partners in grace with him.
True or false: When Paul talks about how much he longs for the believers at Philippi, he calls Timothy as his witness.

cards.text: Then Paul gets to the big one: "And this is my prayer:" that their love would grow more and more. Not "that's plenty," not "let's cap it here," friend, MORE AND MORE.

cards.question: Paul prays the love of the believers at Philippi will abound more and more. In what?

cards.text: Now Paul says what love like that is for. Because love with no insight is me, my first week in this bakery, putting sprinkles on EVERYTHING, friend, including my own hat.

cards.question: Paul prays their growing love helps them test and prove what is ___, so they'll be pure and blameless for the day of Christ

cards.text: Last part of Paul's prayer: he wants them filled with the fruit of righteousness. That's not a topping, friend, so put the mango bits down.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the fruit of righteousness he wants the believers at Philippi filled with comes through their own hard work.
Paul ends his prayer by saying all of it is to the glory and praise of whom?

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Next, Paul says what he's sure of…', 'Me?', 'I started building a cooling rack…' and 'It's always gonna be a shelf.' Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Philippians 1:8. Paul's longing, God as his witness and the affection of Christ Jesus are never told. The baker has to guess whether Timothy is the witness, and Timothy co-sent the letter, so True looks plausible. Because the answer is False, the baker also never learns who Paul's witness actually is.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 13 sets up 'that their love would grow more and more,' and card 14 asks for the rest of the line ('in knowledge and depth of insight'). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason this out over 'Strength and endurance.' It asks the baker to guess the wording of the line, not its meaning. The 'love with no insight' setup comes after the question, on card 15.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
